summary: This script generates a diagram of a Kubernetes stateful application architecture. It creates a visual representation showing a service routing to three pods, each with its own persistent volume claim, all backed by a shared persistent volume and storage class. The diagram is built using the diagrams library and saved to a file rather than displayed immediately.

explanations.6: The Diagram context manager creates a new diagram document titled 'Stateful Architecture'; show=False means it will save to a file instead of opening in a window.
explanations.7: Cluster groups related components together visually in the diagram, like putting them in a box labeled 'Apps'.
explanations.12: The loop runs three times (range(3)), creating three separate pod-and-storage combinations to represent replicas in the stateful set.
explanations.15: The minus operator (-) and right-shift operator (>>) are used to draw connections between components; this line connects pod to statefulset to pvc.
explanations.16: This appends a chain of connections to the apps list—showing that the service routes to the pod, which routes to the pvc; the >> operator draws directional arrows.
explanations.18: This line connects everything in the apps list to a shared PV, which is connected to the StorageClass; the << operator draws arrows pointing backward (from right to left).
